content.tex: The sum of two different triangle numbers sometimes equals another triangle number. When this happens, we have a triangle triple.

Example \(\bullet\) Start with the triangle number \(T_{3}\quad = 6\) . \(\bullet\) From the table in question 2(a) \(T_{6} -T_{5} = 6\) . So \(T_{6} -T_{5} = T_{3}\) . \(\bullet\) Rearrange the equation \(T_{3} +T_{5} = T_{6}\) . \(\bullet\) The triangle triple is then \((3, 5, 6).\)
The three different numbers must be written in order of increasing size.
